Inversion Count with Updates

An array of N integers is part of a financial anomaly detector. An inversion is a pair of indices (i, j) where i < j but arr[i] > arr[j], suggesting a market anomaly. You must dynamically maintain the inversion count as individual elements are updated.

You receive Q operations:

Type 1: 1 i x — Update arr[i] (1-indexed) to value x.

Type 2: 2 — Output the current total inversion count.
explanation: For the initial count, use merge sort in O(N log N). For each point update, locally recompute the change in inversions by counting how many elements to the left of the updated position are greater than the new value, and how many to the right are smaller. This gives the delta change in inversions. Using a BIT on coordinate-compressed values can make each query and update O(log N) rather than O(N). Overall time: O(N log N + Q log N).
